lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The corridor door. Shut, as doors here are, and your card still opens it.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: The quarter is not closed. I have never walked out on an open quarter in eleven years and I am not going to start tonight, which I am aware is a strange thing to be proud of.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The door, and behind it a corridor lit end to end. The card reader is dark. The door is not locked — it has simply stopped being yours, which in this century is the same thing and takes less paperwork.

choices.text: Go. Down the stairs, out the service side, up the valley road.
